title.text: A Fruitcake-Spiced Canna-Cocktail Without the Booze

dek: Black tea, cranberry and berry preserves with orange peel and warm spice: an alcohol-free holiday glass with a measured THC tincture shaken in.
pictureAlt: A ruby spiced mocktail in a rocks glass over ice with an orange peel twist and cherries, cinnamon dusted on the table

runs: Chilled black tea, cranberry juice and cherry or blueberry preserves bring fruitcake's dark-fruit depth.
Read the tincture label, start low, and shake the dose in before the ice so it mixes through.
It's alcohol-free by design; top it with berry seltzer for a sparkling version.
Mix the same base without tincture so every guest gets a festive glass.

items.text: Shake, strain, serve your holiday THC mocktail
A zero-THC glass for everyone else

runs: This holiday THC mocktail earns its fruitcake name. It starts as a black tea mocktail, with cranberry juice and berry preserves for dark-fruit depth. Orange peel and a pinch of warm spice add the bakery notes, and a measured THC tincture is shaken right in. There's no liquor, just a festive glass that tastes like the holidays.

The dose comes from the tincture, so read its label first: it lists THC in mg per ml. Measure with the marked dropper or a small oral syringe, and start low. Health Canada suggests new consumers begin at 2.5 mg of THC or less. Shake the tincture with the tea, juice and preserves before any ice goes in, so it mixes through the whole drink. Then give it at least 2 hours before a second glass.

body.text: Shake, strain, serve your holiday THC mocktail

runs: Shake everything with the tincture until the preserves dissolve, add ice and shake again, then strain over fresh ice. Twist the orange peel over the glass and drop it in with the cherries. For a sparkling version, strain into a tall glass and top with berry seltzer.

Mix to order when you can, so each glass gets its own measured dose. If you batch a pitcher, stir the total tincture dose in thoroughly, label the pitcher 'contains THC' with the dose per cup, and serve it with a measuring cup. Pour out whatever remains once the party winds down instead of saving it, and keep tinctures away from children and pets. If someone drinks an infused glass by accident, call Poison Control at 1-800-222-1222.

body.text: A zero-THC glass for everyone else

runs: Make the same base without tincture in a second, clearly marked pitcher, so every guest gets the fruitcake glass. Keep the infused version for adults 21+ who know what's in it, and make sure nobody who drinks it drives.

4 ounces strong black tea, regular or decaf, brewed and chilled
2 ounces cranberry juice
1 tablespoon cherry or blueberry preserves
1 wide strip of orange peel
1 small pinch of cinnamon, allspice or nutmeg
THC tincture, measured for 1 serving (see the dosing note)
Ice
2 dried or maraschino cherries
Optional: 2 to 3 ounces berry seltzer
Combine the tea, cranberry juice, preserves, spice and measured tincture in a cocktail shaker or a jar with a tight lid.
Shake hard for about 10 seconds, until the preserves have dissolved.
Add a handful of ice and shake for another 10 seconds.
Strain into a rocks glass over fresh ice. Twist the orange peel over the drink, then drop it in with the cherries.
For a sparkling version, strain into a tall glass of ice instead and top with berry seltzer.

ml of tincture × the label's mg per ml = THC in the drink. Example: 1 ml of a tincture labeled 3 mg per ml is about 3 mg. A homemade tincture is an estimate that depends on the flower's potency and on decarboxylation and extraction losses. Start low, wait at least 2 hours before a second, label any batched pitcher, and keep infused drinks away from children and pets.

items.q: How much tincture goes in one mocktail?

runs: Enough for the dose you chose, measured in milliliters. Multiply the ml you add by the label's mg per ml: 1 ml of a tincture labeled 3 mg per ml is about 3 mg, for example. Keep the first glass small, and wait at least 2 hours before deciding on another.

Yes. Decaf black tea keeps the same malty backbone with only a trace of caffeine, which makes the glass easier to enjoy late in the evening. Brew it strong, since ice and juice dilute it, and chill it completely before mixing. Rooibos works too, for a naturally caffeine-free glass with a warm, slightly sweet flavor.

items.q: Does caffeine change how THC feels?

runs: It might, and there's no reliable way to predict how it will for you. Caffeine is a stimulant, and THC affects people differently, so the pairing can feel different from one person to the next. To keep things simple, brew decaf, so the THC you measured is the one new variable in your glass.
